info.name: ALLURA API
info.description:
Backend API collection for the ALLURA admin + mobile clients.

## How to use

1. Import this collection into Postman.
2. Set `base_url` in **Collection Variables** (already defaults to `http://ALLURA-upgradation.test` for local dev).
3. Run **Auth → Login** once with a real admin email/password — the post-response script stores `access_token` + `refresh_token` on the collection.
4. Every other request inherits `Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}}` from collection-level auth.
5. Access tokens expire in 15 minutes; run **Auth → Refresh** to rotate without re-entering credentials.

## Scope

- Auth (Passport password grant — v2)
- Application Users (CRUD, status, password change)
- Roles (CRUD + duplicate)
- Permissions (CRUD + parent groups)

More modules will be appended as they're requested.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Passport password-grant auth. Login stores access + refresh tokens on the collection so every other request authenticates automatically.

request.description:
Exchanges email + password for a Passport access/refresh pair. Rate-limited 5/min.

Response `data`: `{ access_token, refresh_token, expires_in, token_type, user }`.

exec: console.log('Stored access + refresh tokens on collection.');

request.description: Rotates the access + refresh token pair. Rate-limited 10/min.
Revokes the current access token and its refresh chain.

item.name: Users
item.description:
Application (staff/admin) users — CRUD, status toggle, password change.

`/api/users/datatable` returns a DataTables-style payload outside the standard envelope; on the SPA side call `api.post(path, body, { raw: true })`.

request.description: Paginated list with filters. Permission: `users_manage`.
Returns roles, locations, warehouses, user types needed to render the create form. Permission: `users_create`.
Password must be 8+ chars with upper, lower, digit, and special char. Permission: `users_create`.
User data + dropdowns for the edit form. Permission: `users_edit`.
Full user update. `email`, `phone`, `gender` required on PUT/PATCH. Permission: `users_edit`.
Soft-delete user. Permission: `users_destroy`.
Activate (status=1) or deactivate (status=0) a user. Permission: `users_active`.

variable.description: Encrypted user id — obtain from a previous endpoint, not the raw integer in production.

request.description: Returns the encrypted id used by the PATCH below. Permission: `users_change_password`.
⚠️ Current known auth gap: no re-auth / current_password check. Permission: `users_change_password`.

Permission: `roles_duplicate`.

item.name: Doctors
item.description: Doctor management — Doctors are a User subtype (`user_type_id = 5`) with a parallel `resources` row (`resource_type_id = 2`) for rotation/scheduling. The API lives under `/api/doctors/*`. Dashboard endpoints under `/api/doctor-dashboard/*` are for the doctor's own KPI view (gated by role, not a dedicated permission). Lookup endpoints (`/api/appointments/load-*`, `/api/get-doctors*`) are used by appointment and sales flows to pick a doctor.

request.description: Paginated doctor list. Filterable by name/email/phone/gender/role/status/date. Permission: `doctors_manage`.
Returns roles, locations, and service hierarchy needed to render the create form. Permission: `doctors_create`.
Creates a doctor (User with `user_type_id = 5` plus a Resources row). Password must be 8+ chars with upper, lower, digit, special char. Permission: `doctors_create`.
Returns the doctor + current location/service allocations + dropdown options for the edit form. Permission: `doctors_edit`.
Update doctor profile. `password` optional on update (omit to keep current). Permission: `doctors_edit`.
Soft-delete doctor. Also drives the datatable bulk-delete action when the SPA sends an id array. Permission: `doctors_destroy`.
Activate (`status=1`) or deactivate (`status=0`) a doctor. Two separate permissions — `doctors_active` for activation, `doctors_inactive` for deactivation.

variable.description: Encrypted doctor id used by the PATCH below.

request.description: Returns the encrypted id used when saving the new password. Permission: `doctors_change_password`.
Same no-re-auth caveat as the users endpoint. Permission: `doctors_change_password`.
Returns the location allocation list (allocated + available locations with `is_allocated` flag). Permission: `doctors_allocate`.
Returns the service tree for a given doctor + location showing which services are allocated. Permission: `doctors_allocate`.
Allocates services to a doctor for a location (persists to `doctor_has_locations` pivot). Permission: `doctors_allocate`.
Unallocates services from a doctor for a location. Permission: `doctors_allocate`.
Doctor-facing KPI metrics for the signed-in doctor. Gated by role (`Aesthetic Doctor` / `Lifestyle Consultant`) — not a dedicated permission.
Hero summary section for the doctor dashboard.
Today's appointments for the signed-in doctor.
Benchmark comparison data (⚠️ audit noted this method existence wasn't fully verified — may need backend confirmation).
Minimal `{id, name}` list for dropdown pickers (admin-config).
Doctors available for a given location/service/date — used by the appointment booking flow.
Doctors with `can_perform_consultation = 1` for a location.
Working hours / off days for a doctor on a given date.
Doctor picker for the sales/orders flow.
Generic doctor list (orders module).

item.name: User Types

Seeded values include Doctor (5), Patient (3), etc. Full CRUD + an active/inactive split using PATCH-by-id (NOT the POST `/status` pattern used by users and doctors). Dropdown + doctor-list helpers for pickers elsewhere in the app.

request.description: Paginated list. Permission: `user_types_manage`.
Dropdown / init data for the create form. Permission: `user_types_create`.
Permission: `user_types_create`.
Permission: `user_types_manage`.
Permission: `user_types_edit`.
Permission: `user_types_edit`.
Permission: `user_types_destroy`.

item.name: Regions
item.description:
Per-account regions (top level of the Region → City → Location hierarchy). The root `slug='all'` row is internal and never exposed by REST. User-created regions all have `slug='custom'` and carry a `sort_number`.

Permissions: `regions_manage` (read), `regions_create`, `regions_edit`, `regions_active`, `regions_inactive`, `regions_sort`, `regions_destroy`. Callers lacking `view_inactive_regions` see active rows only.

The REST endpoints below add `index`, `show`, `PATCH update`, `PATCH status`, `dropdown`, `sorted`, and `POST sort` on top of the legacy datatable/PUT/POST-store/DELETE endpoints. Legacy URIs remain live so the admin UI keeps working — REST consumers should prefer the new endpoints.

query.description: 0 = inactive, 1 = active. Admin-only filter (needs `view_inactive_regions`); otherwise callers only ever see active rows.

request.description: Paginated `RegionResource` list, ordered by `sort_number` asc. Only `slug='custom'` rows. Each row exposes `locations_count` + `active_locations_count`. Permission: `regions_manage`.
Active regions as `{ id, name }[]` in sort order — the shape mobile pickers expect. Permission: `regions_manage`.
Full region list in `sort_number` order — used to seed the drag-and-drop reorder UI. Permission: `regions_sort`.
Bulk reorder — the resulting `sort_number` is the array index (0 for the first id). REST wrapper around `RegionService::saveSortOrder`. Permission: `regions_sort`.
Detail for a single region with `locations_count` + `active_locations_count`. Cross-account rows return 404. Permission: `regions_manage`.

Update name / active flag. `name` unique per account (scoped to `slug='custom'`, soft-deletes ignored). Root region (`slug='all'`) cannot be modified — returns 422. Delegates to `Regions::updateRecord` so audit trail + widget hooks fire. Permission: `regions_edit`.
Activate (`status=1`) or deactivate (`status=0`). Gated by `regions_active` / `regions_inactive` respectively (enforced in the Form Request `authorize`). Root region cannot be deactivated — 422.

Create a region. Legacy route — calls `Admin\RegionsController@store` → `RegionService::validateAndCreate` which only requires `name`. Legacy UI relies on this for the create flow. Permission: `regions_create`.

Legacy PUT — same side effects as the REST PATCH but no uniqueness validation, no `JsonResource` response. Prefer the REST `PATCH /api/regions/{region}` for new integrations. Permission: `regions_edit`.

Soft-delete via `Regions::DeleteRecord`. **Guards:** root region (`slug='all'`) → 422; region with linked Leads or Appointments → 409. Cities + Locations under the region are cascade-deleted inside the service (preserved exactly from legacy). Permission: `regions_destroy`.
Legacy POST — takes the `id` in the body. Prefer the REST `PATCH /api/regions/{region}/status` for new integrations. Gated by `regions_active` / `regions_inactive`.
Legacy KTDatatable-protocol list. Prefer the REST `list` endpoint. Permission: `regions_manage`.
Legacy fetch-for-edit endpoint used by the admin UI. Prefer the REST `show` endpoint. Permission: `regions_edit`.
Legacy sort-list. Prefer the REST `GET /api/regions/sorted`. Permission: `regions_sort`.
Legacy bulk reorder. Prefer the REST `POST /api/regions/sort`. Permission: `regions_sort`.

item.name: Operator Settings
item.description:
Per-account configuration for external operator/gateway integrations (e.g. SMS, comms providers). Two tables back this module:

- `global_operator_settings` — read-only templates shared across accounts (the list of supported operators).
- `user_operator_settings` — the caller's account-scoped credentials + per-account overrides (URL, username, password, mask, sandbox flag, extra string fields).

Permissions: `user_operator_settings_manage` (read), `user_operator_settings_edit` (write). Password is encrypted at rest (`EncryptedLegacy` cast) and is **always masked** in responses — credentials never leave the server. Sending an empty/missing `password` on update preserves the existing one.

The legacy datatable endpoint (`POST /api/user_operator_settings/datatable` + `GET /{id}/edit` + `PUT /{id}`) is kept for the admin UI. The REST endpoints below are the mobile- and integration-friendly surface.

request.description: Paginated `OperatorSettingResource` list scoped to the caller's account, ordered by `operator_name` asc. Permission: `user_operator_settings_manage`.
Detail for a single user-operator row. Password is masked (`********`). Cross-account rows return 404. Permission: `user_operator_settings_manage`.

Partial update — every field is optional. **`password` empty/omitted preserves the existing value** (so clients can safely re-submit a form without re-typing the secret). `test_mode` is an integer (`0` or `1`). Audit-logged via the existing `UserOperatorSettingsService::update` path. Permission: `user_operator_settings_edit`.
Convenience endpoint — flip between sandbox (`1`) and live (`0`) without re-sending every field. Permission: `user_operator_settings_edit`.

Read-only list of `global_operator_settings` templates — the supported operators across all accounts. Use when populating a picker before cloning a template into the account. Permission: `user_operator_settings_manage`.
Single global template. Replaces the legacy `loadOperator` POST endpoint — same payload, REST-friendly method + path. Password masked. Permission: `user_operator_settings_manage`.
Legacy KTDatatable-protocol list. Prefer the REST `list` endpoint above for new integrations. Permission: `user_operator_settings_manage`.
Legacy fetch-for-edit endpoint. Returns the raw model (password masked by the model's `$hidden`). Prefer the REST `show` endpoint. Permission: `user_operator_settings_edit`.

Legacy PUT update — **requires `test_mode`** even on partial changes. New integrations should prefer the REST `PATCH /api/operator-settings/{id}` endpoint which allows true partial updates and preserves existing passwords on empty submit. Permission: `user_operator_settings_manage`.

item.name: Business Working Days
item.description:
Weekly open/closed pattern + per-date exceptions. Stored as: (1) a `settings` row keyed by `slug=business_working_days` holding the 7-day map; (2) a `working_day_exceptions` row per overriding date.

Permission: `schedule_manage`. Defaults to Mon–Sat open / Sun closed when nothing has been saved yet. The legacy `/api/schedule/get-business-working-days` + `/api/schedule/save-business-working-days` endpoints stay for the admin UI — the REST endpoints below are the preferred surface and split the concerns (pattern vs. exceptions) so callers can update one without wiping the other.

request.description: Current 7-day weekly pattern + every saved exception. Response: `{ working_days: {monday..sunday: bool}, exceptions: WorkingDayExceptionResource[] }`. Falls back to Mon–Sat open / Sun closed when nothing is saved. Permission: `schedule_manage`.

Update the weekly pattern only — every day is **required**. Unlike the legacy `save-business-working-days` this **does not touch** the exceptions list; use the `/exceptions` sub-resource for that. Permission: `schedule_manage`.

Is the business open on this date? Exception override wins over the weekly pattern. Response: `{ date, day_of_week, is_working, is_exception, exception: WorkingDayExceptionResource | null }`. Permission: `schedule_manage`.
Per-date open/closed for a range (max 365 days). Each day entry: `{ date, day_of_week, is_working, is_exception, exception_title }`. Designed for mobile calendar dots. Permission: `schedule_manage`.
All override-dates for the account, oldest first, with the creator eager-loaded. Permission: `schedule_manage`.

Idempotent — a second call for the same `exception_date` updates the existing row. Returns 201 on create, 200 on update. `is_working=true` = make a normally-closed day open; `false` = make an open day closed. Permission: `schedule_manage`.
Single exception detail. Cross-account rows return 404. Permission: `schedule_manage`.
Partial update — all fields optional. Permission: `schedule_manage`.
Remove a single exception — the date then falls back to the weekly pattern. Permission: `schedule_manage`.

**Replace-all** semantics — deletes every existing exception for the account and inserts the new set inside a `DB::transaction`. Mirrors the legacy `/schedule/save-business-working-days` exception handling but as a standalone endpoint. `exceptions` may be empty (clears everything). Max 365 rows; `exception_date`s must be distinct. Permission: `schedule_manage`.

Legacy endpoint used by the admin Settings page. Same payload as the REST `show` endpoint but exceptions come back as a flat array with formatted date strings. Prefer the REST endpoint for new integrations.

**Legacy combined save** — wipes all exceptions and recreates them every call. Use the REST endpoints above if you want to update only the pattern OR only specific exceptions without touching the other. Kept for admin UI compatibility.

item.name: Business Closures
item.description:
Business closure periods (multi-day store-wide or location-specific shutdowns). Permissions: `business_closures_manage` (read + parent), `business_closures_create`, `business_closures_edit`, `business_closures_delete`.

The legacy endpoints (datatable / create / edit / update / destroy) stay for the admin web UI. The REST endpoints below (list / show / upcoming / check / bulk-delete) are the mobile- and integration-friendly surface, returning `BusinessClosureResource` with locations + creator eager-loaded.

query.description: Optional. Matches closures that either cover this location or are account-wide (no locations attached).
ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD). Returns closures ending on/after this date.
ISO date. Returns closures starting on/before this date.

request.description: Paginated `BusinessClosureResource` list with locations + creator eager-loaded. Newest `start_date` first. Account-scoped via `Auth::user()->account_id`. Permission: `business_closures_manage`.

query.description: Optional location scope (matches location-specific + account-wide closures).

request.description: Closures overlapping the next `days` window, ordered by `start_date` asc. Response: `{ window_days, from, to, items[] }`. Permission: `business_closures_manage`.

Is the business closed on a given date? Intended for pre-booking checks. Returns `{ date, location_id, is_closed, closures[] }` — `is_closed=true` when any closure matches. Omitting `location_id` checks all closures for the account. Permission: `business_closures_manage`.

REST detail — pure `BusinessClosureResource` shape with locations + creator. Unlike `/{id}/edit`, does not include the locations dropdown. Cross-account rows return 404. Permission: `business_closures_manage`.
Returns the active-locations dropdown for the create form. ACL-scoped to the caller's allowed centres. Permission: `business_closures_create`.

Create closure. `location_ids` required — pass `["all"]` (string literal) to mark account-wide (service treats any entry of `"all"` as no-locations-attached). Wrapped in `DB::transaction` with `AuditTrails` logging. Permission: `business_closures_create`.
Returns `{ closure, location_ids, locations }` — includes the dropdown the edit form needs. Permission: `business_closures_edit`.
Update closure. `location_ids` with a single `"all"` entry clears all attachments (account-wide). Permission: `business_closures_edit`.
Soft-delete a single closure. Account-scoped via `firstOrFail`. Permission: `business_closures_delete`.

Clean REST wrapper around `BusinessClosureService::bulkDelete`. `ids` must be 1–500 distinct integers. Cross-account ids are silently skipped (service enforces account scope per row). Returns `{ deleted_count }`. Permission: `business_closures_delete`.

Legacy datatable endpoint (DataTables-protocol body, KTDatatable-shaped response). Prefer the REST `list` endpoint above for new integrations. Also accepts a `delete` filter with a comma-separated id list for legacy bulk-delete (prefer the dedicated `bulk-delete` endpoint). Permission: `business_closures_manage`.

item.name: HRM
item.description:
HRM module — employee management, leave mgmt, recruitment, notifications, self-service. Fiscal year is Jul–Jun (formatted `YYYY-YY`, e.g. `2025-26`). Leave durations are typed enums: Full=1.0, Half=0.5, Short=0.25.

**Current API surface is limited**: 4 datatables + 1 calendar feed + 3 notification endpoints. Employee CRUD, leave approve/reject/cancel, recruitment CRUD, and self-service flows are web-only today (`/hr/*`) and need API wrappers. See the backlog in `docs/audits/` (coming) for the build list.

query.description: 1–50. Max pending leaves in the response. Defaults to 10.
1–90. Upcoming-leaves window in days. Defaults to 7.
1–365. Recent-hires window in days. Defaults to 30.

request.description: Unified HRM dashboard payload: `{ kpis, pending_leaves[], upcoming_leaves[], recent_hires[], generated_at }`. Mirrors the web dashboard view plus two mobile-friendly extras (upcoming leaves + recent hires). Permission: `hr_dashboard_view`.

Lightweight counts only: `{ total_employees, pending_leaves, approved_this_month, open_candidates, on_leave_today }`. Use this for pull-to-refresh when the full dashboard payload is overkill. Permission: `hr_dashboard_view`.

Paginated list of all pending leave applications for the caller's account, most recent first. Each item is a `LeaveApplicationResource` with the applicant + designation + leave type eager-loaded. Permission: `hr_dashboard_view`.

query.description: 1–90; window size in days. Defaults to 7.

request.description: Approved leaves starting within the next `days` window, ordered by `start_date` asc. Useful for roster planning. Permission: `hr_dashboard_view`.

query.description: 1–365; window size in days. Defaults to 30.

request.description: Employees whose `employee_details.hire_date` falls within the last `days`, most recent first (max 20). Response item shape: `{ id, name, designation, department, hire_date }`. Permission: `hr_dashboard_view`.
Paginated employee list. Filters: `name`, `designation`, `status`, `location_id`. Permission: `hr_employees_view`.
Paginated leave applications. Filters: `status`, `leave_type`, `employee_name`, `date_from`, `date_to`. Permission: `hr_leave_view`.
Leave balance by employee for a fiscal year (`YYYY-YY` format — e.g. `2025-26`). Permission: `hr_leave_view`.
Paginated candidates. `status` enum: `scheduled, in_review, shortlisted, on_hold, offer, hired, offer_declined, rejected, blacklisted`. Permission: `hr_recruitment_view`.

query.description: Optional. `scheduled | in_review | shortlisted | on_hold | offer | hired | offer_declined | rejected | blacklisted`.
`true` to constrain to open pipeline statuses (scheduled / in_review / shortlisted / on_hold / offer).

request.description: Paginated `RecruitmentCandidateResource` list with designation, city, location, converted user eager-loaded and `interviews_count` attached. Permission: `hr_recruitment_view`.
Candidate counts keyed by status plus `open` + `total`. Drives the recruitment pipeline widget / badge counter. Permission: `hr_recruitment_view`.

formdata.description: Optional. PDF / DOC / DOCX, max 5 MB. Stored on the `r2` disk under `accounts/{account_id}/hr/recruitment`.

request.description: Creates the candidate AND schedules the first interview in one transaction (matches the legacy business rule). Status starts at `scheduled`. Multipart form; `cv` is optional. Permission: `hr_recruitment_create`. Returns `RecruitmentCandidateResource` (201).
Candidate detail with designation, city, location, interviews (+ interviewer), and converted user. Cross-account rows return 404. Permission: `hr_recruitment_view`.

formdata.description: Optional. Replacing a CV deletes the previous file from R2.

request.description: Update candidate profile. A new `cv` replaces the existing file; the old object is deleted from R2. Permission: `hr_recruitment_edit`.
Transition candidate status. Allowed values: `scheduled, in_review, shortlisted, on_hold, offer, hired, offer_declined, rejected, blacklisted`. Permission: `hr_recruitment_status_update`.
Streams the CV binary with `Content-Disposition: inline` for in-browser preview. 404 if the candidate has no CV on file. Permission: `hr_recruitment_view`.
Same stream as preview but served with `Content-Disposition: attachment` so clients save the file. Permission: `hr_recruitment_view`.

Creates a `User` + `EmployeeDetail`, assigns the optional role and the candidate's location (via `user_has_locations`), then flips the candidate to `hired` with `converted_user_id` set. Wrapped in one transaction via `RecruitmentService::convertToEmployee`. Returns **409** if already converted. Permission: `hr_recruitment_convert`.
Soft-delete. Returns **409** if the candidate has already been converted to an employee (preserves the hire audit trail). Permission: `hr_recruitment_delete`.
All interview rounds for a candidate, newest first. Each row includes the scorecard, average score, verdict, and interviewer. Permission: `hr_recruitment_view`.

Add a new interview round under the candidate. If a scorecard or verdict is submitted and the candidate is still `scheduled`, the candidate is auto-transitioned to `in_review` (mirrors legacy behaviour). Scores are 1–5. Permission: `hr_recruitment_interview_manage`.
Legacy-compatible flat endpoint: same as the nested version but `candidate_id` lives in the body. Same permission and auto-transition behaviour. Permission: `hr_recruitment_interview_manage`.

Edit scorecard / notes / schedule. All fields are optional — partial updates supported. Submitting a scorecard still triggers the `scheduled → in_review` auto-transition. Permission: `hr_recruitment_interview_manage`.
Remove an interview round. Cross-account rows return 404. Permission: `hr_recruitment_interview_manage`.
Approved/pending leave events for the vis-timeline calendar. Permission: `hr_leave_view`.
Signed-in user's recent HR notifications. Returns `{ notifications, unread_count }`. No permission gate — scoped to the current user.
Marks a single notification read. Ownership enforced in the controller.
Marks every notification for the current user as read.
Create employee (User + EmployeeDetail + location assignment in one transaction). Permission: `hr_employees_manage`. Returns `EmployeeResource` with 201.
Full employee profile with EmployeeDetail, documents, locations. Permission: `hr_employees_view`.
Update employee. `password` omitted keeps current. Permission: `hr_employees_manage`.
Soft-delete employee. Also revokes the user's Sanctum tokens so any live session dies. Permission: `hr_employees_manage`.
Activate (`status=1`) or deactivate (`status=0`). Response: `{ id, active }`. Permission: `hr_employees_manage`.

query.description: Admin-only filter. Non-admins are force-scoped to their own rows regardless.
Name search. Ignored for non-admin callers.

request.description: Paginated leave applications with employee + designation + leave type + reviewer eager-loaded. Callers without `hr_leave_view` are auto-scoped to their own applications — no 403. Response: `{ items, meta }` where each item is a `LeaveApplicationResource`.

body.raw:
{
  "user_id": 1,
  "leave_type_id": 1,
  "start_date": "2026-05-10",
  "end_date": "2026-05-12",
  "duration_type": "full",
  "custom_hours": null,
  "reason": "Applied on behalf — pre-planned vacation.",
  "auto_approve": false,
  "review_notes": null
}

request.description: HR creates a leave application on behalf of an employee. Reuses `LeaveService::apply` so overlap / shift-hour / balance checks stay centralised. Returns **409** on overlapping dates. `auto_approve=true` approves immediately and increments the balance. `duration_type`: `full` | `half` | `short` | `custom` (requires `custom_hours > 0`). Permission: `hr_leave_approve`.
Status counts for dashboards and badges: `{ pending, approved, rejected, cancelled, total }`. Filters apply to `start_date` within the window. Permission: `hr_leave_view`.

Month-scoped pending + approved applications for a calendar grid. Returns `{ month, year, items[] }` where each item is `{ id, user_id, user_name, leave_type, status, start_date, end_date, total_days }`. Mobile-friendly shape — see `calendar-data` for the legacy Vis-timeline shape. Permission: `hr_leave_view`.

Streams a CSV named `leave_applications_{timestamp}.csv` with columns: ID, Employee, Leave Type, Start Date, End Date, Duration, Total Days, Status, Reason, Applied On. Uses `chunkById(500)` so it stays safe on production-sized tables. Permission: `hr_leave_view`.
Application detail with reviewer, notes, leave type, and employee. Access: the applicant OR anyone with `hr_leave_view`.
`review_notes` optional. Permission: `hr_leave_approve`.
`review_notes` **required** (max 1000). Permission: `hr_leave_approve`.

Mirrors the web rule exactly: **pending** leave → applicant or `hr_leave_approve` can cancel; **approved** leave → only `hr_leave_approve` (not the applicant). Leave balance is refunded via the existing service.
Own profile (User + EmployeeDetail + locations + documents). No permission required — ownership via `Auth::id()`. Null-safe when no EmployeeDetail exists.

Allowlist-only: `phone`, `dob`, `gender`, `address`, emergency contact fields. Any other field (salary, department, manager, active) is silently dropped. If the user has no EmployeeDetail row, emergency-contact fields no-op (documented ALLURA-REVIEW).
Own balances (current fiscal year, `YYYY-YY`) + applications + shift_hours in one response.

`duration` enum: `full` (1.0) / `half` (0.5) / `short` (0.25) / `custom` (requires `custom_hours`). Overlap-checked and balance-warned via the existing `LeaveService`. Returns `LeaveApplicationResource` (201).
Edit own pending leave. 403 if not the applicant, 422 if status != pending.
Cancel own pending leave. Rejects approved leaves with 422 (that path is HR-only via `/leave-applications/{id}/cancel`).
Own employee documents with Google Drive upload status. Returns `EmployeeDocumentResource::collection`.

Account-scoped departments ordered by name. Callers with `hr_departments_manage` also see inactive entries; without it only active rows are returned. Each row includes `designations_count` and `employees_count`. Permission: `hr_departments_view`.
Single department with counts. 404 if the department belongs to a different account. Permission: `hr_departments_view`.

Create a department. `name` is required and must be unique per account (excluding soft-deleted rows). `active` defaults to `true`. Permission: `hr_departments_manage`. Returns `DepartmentResource` (201).
Update department name / active flag. Cross-account updates return 404. Permission: `hr_departments_manage`.
